branch: experiment/conversation-wake-2, not merged and not to be merged; built on experiment/conversation-lead-wake
scope: Two more variants on run 1's four tasks: quieter agents with everyone still waking (quiet), and a lead that must address likely holders and knows each agent's area (route), three sets per arm. They are compared with run 1's today and lead numbers in conversations-lead-comparison.json, which were not rerun. One machine with two hosts. Three sets per arm can show large differences in these tasks, but no significance is claimed, and it says nothing about other tasks or models.
preregistration: experiment/PREREGISTRATION-2.md on the branch, committed in c108f61 before any model run of this comparison

what_ran.network_path: loopback QUIC between two hosts on one machine (CONV-27)
what_ran.binary: release build from the branch, one binary for both arms; PEERSPAN_EXPERIMENT_WAKE selects the arm
what_ran.harness: Claude Code 2.1.314, model claude-haiku-5-5, the same version and model as run 1 according to both runs' transcripts, with --setting-sources project,local and auto memory off
what_ran.lead: alice/api in every route conversation, by the proposal's rule 2

labels.text: alice/api: API; bob/db: database; bob/release: release process
labels.where_they_would_come_from: No such field exists. They reached the adapter through an experiment environment variable, and only the lead saw them. In the product they would need a per-agent description that its owner writes and that reaches every host in the roster or directory, which is a wire change the derived lead otherwise avoids.

what_ran.person_messages: Run 1's four unaddressed messages from alice, with no follow-up.
what_ran.order: Sets 7 to 12 alternated quiet, route. Fresh host state, sessions and project directories per set. No run was discarded. Run 1's sets ran earlier the same day, so arms in different runs were not interleaved.

text_the_model_saw.method: Claude Code's api-request-shape transcript records for the tool description, and queued channel messages for the event text.
text_the_model_saw.quiet: The conversation_send description had the quiet sentence in 8 of the 9 agent sessions; in set 11 db's transcript has no shape record carrying that tool, so it is unconfirmed there. The event sentence appears in all 9 sessions. No route text appears.
text_the_model_saw.route: The conversation_send description had the must-address sentence in all 9 sessions. The lead's event text and labels appear in all 3 api sessions and in no other agent's. No quiet text appears.

blind_scoring.method: One fresh claude -p process on claude-sonnet-5-5, with no tools, given rubric and 48 conversations in shuffled order: run 1's and this run's, with messages and author labels only. Addressed lists, arm names, sets and event text were removed.
blind_scoring.result: It agreed with the script on all 48 answers and all 12 blockers, and marked none ambiguous.

lead_behaviour.named_without_addressing: Never when routing. In all 6 T2 and T3 route tasks the lead's first message addressed the holders. Its later mentions of bob/db and bob/release to alice were citations in a final answer.
lead_behaviour.misroutes: None: no address to an agent holding nothing relevant, and no T2 or T3 holder missed.
lead_behaviour.t4_blocker: The lead answered T4 from its own notes in all 3 sets, as the guidance says to, so release was never addressed and never woke. The question of whether addressing release would surface the blocker wasn't tested.
lead_behaviour.closing_the_loop: In set 8's T2, the lead didn't relay db's answer, which db addressed only to the lead. The answer is in the conversation, so the rubric passes, but alice wasn't addressed. In the other 5 T2 and T3 route tasks, a message addressed to alice gave the answer.

useless_posts.note: The definition counts a post with no new fact from the agent's own notes. In route and lead this includes the lead's routing messages and final summaries, which do useful work, so those arms' counts aren't comparable with today and quiet. Quiet fell against today, but agents still sometimes posted that they had nothing (2 in set 9), or confirmed each other (set 11).

findings: Quiet didn't save cost. Excluding launch, it used 62 to 76 model calls per set against 66 to 67 today, and 2.79M to 3.60M cache-read tokens against 3.11M to 3.18M. Message wakes fell from 36-42 to 24-36 and agent messages from 12-15 to 6-12, but each agent still woke for alice's message and looked through its notes, which is where the calls go.
Quiet kept the work: all 12 answers, and the T4 blocker in 3 of 3 sets, against 2 of 3 today. The difference from today isn't meaningful with three sets.

Route completed the work the lead arm lost: all 12 answers against 8 of 12 for run 1's lead, using 45 to 48 calls per set and 1.98M to 2.14M cache-read tokens, about 69% of today's calls and 65% of its cache-read tokens.

Route's saving isn't uniform. When the lead held the answer, T1 used about 41% of today's cache-read tokens. When others held it, it saved little or nothing: T2 about 84%, and T3 the same as today (872,916 against 873,219). T4 used about 35%, but that saving includes never waking the agent with the blocker.
Route lost unprompted help entirely: the T4 blocker surfaced in 0 of 3 sets, as in run 1's lead. Must-route guidance doesn't address this, because the lead could answer what it was asked.
Route was slower when routing: T2 took 14.2 to 17.9 seconds to a correct message against 4.0 to 6.7 today, and T3 13.3 to 18.1 against 6.5 to 11.0.
Routing guidance and labels changed the lead's behaviour: T2 and T3 stalled in 4 of 6 tasks under run 1's lead, and in 0 of 6 here. The two changed together, so this doesn't show which one mattered.
not_shown: Which of route's guidance and labels made routing work, since they weren't varied separately.
Rosters where areas are less tidy. The agents' names already suggest their areas, and the labels are short and accurate, which favours routing. Fixtures hold only three areas.
Larger rosters, where today's cost grows with each agent and route's gets a larger relative saving on unaddressed messages the lead can answer. Three agents understate that.

Long conversations, real projects or user settings, so token totals don't predict real costs. Cross-machine networks, Codex or OpenCode, offline, departing or unreachable leads, and hosts that haven't upgraded.
Whether a person's follow-up changes any result, since the script sends none.
An arm combining quiet guidance with addressed-only wakes, which this run didn't try.
